Subject: Inference pathways & costing — post-discovery alignment

Alex / team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick post-call recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned. I’ve attached a draft cost model and the mutual action plan.

Highlights from our discussion:
- Target 95p latency: 100-200ms (interactive chat); prefer lower end for customer experience.
- Streaming required: partial token streaming for first-token-to-display UX is mandatory.
- Concurrency profile: steady-state ~200 concurrent active sessions; peak spikes up to ~1k–1.2k for product launches (short duration).
- Average request: 3 prompts / user session, typical prompt length ~80 tokens; responses average ~120 tokens.

Initial asks we agreed on:
1) Helios: share 48 hours of representative traffic (anonymized) + a sample session log so we can simulate real spikes.
2) Redwood (Karthik + Ben): produce two sizing scenarios — a) p95 150ms (higher cost) and b) p95 250ms (lower cost) — with recommended model variants and quantization profiles.
3) Agree on a short POC window (2 weeks) and success criteria: p95 latency target + <=10% token-loss vs baseline quality on a 50-sample eval set.

Cost / performance levers we flagged for evaluation:
- Continuous (micro) batching for throughput efficiency (we’ll show tradeoffs vs latency headroom).
- KV/prefix caching for repeated context across sessions (expected token reduction ~15–25% depending on prompt reuse).
- Quantization options (int8, 4-bit) — we’ll run quality checks and recommend safe profiles.
- Model variant pathing (small-medium-large) and an automated fallback for degraded capacity.

Attachments: 20270601-inference-cost-model.xlsx (draft cost scenarios), mutual_action_plan_v1.md (M.A.P), latency_poc_logs.tar.gz (placeholder).

Proposed next immediate step: technical deep-dive with Karthik + SRE (Ben) tomorrow at 10am PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Thanks Kim — that summary looks right. A couple of clarifications and items attached from our side:

- Concurrency nuance: our peaks are bursty for 60–180s when we push marketing notifications. During a burst we can see 1k–1.2k concurrent active sessions; usual weekday peaks are ~400.
- Streaming detail: we need sub-100ms first-token display on 70% of requests to meet product expectations; rest of tokens can stream at normal pace.
- Quality sensitivity: we can accept small quality diffs for quantized models on causal text generation, but our customer-facing summaries must retain top-k fidelity — recommend we baseline on 50 representative samples.

Alex / Kim — quick technical readout after looking at the sample logs you shared. High-level notes and what I’ll prepare for the POC: 

1) Sizing assumptions we’ll test:
   - Model variants: medium (baseline), medium-quant8 (int8), small-quant4 (4-bit) for fallback.
   - Batching: continuous micro-batching with batch target 8–16; we’ll measure p95 latency impact at 0.5x / 1x / 2x traffic.
   - Caching: prefix-level LRU cache for repeated instructions — expect ~18% token savings on the sample set.

2) Streaming latency details:
   - First-token latency heavily impacted by the scheduler and batch formation window. We can hit sub-100ms first-token in 65–75% of requests when using a small dedicated pool + immediate flush for streaming traffic. Tradeoff: throughput efficiency drops ~8–15%.

3) Quantization & quality risk:
   - int8 (post-training quant) shows ~2–4% BLEU-style delta on our quick eval; 4-bit needs per-model calibration (QAT) but may unlock ~2x memory reduction enabling higher concurrent KV caches.

4) Fallback / routing:
   - Recommend a two-path model policy: route to medium-quant8 under steady state; during spikes route to small-quant4 for throughput; provide transparent header explaining model variant used for auditability.

Deliverables for POC: sizing matrix (latency/cost per SLO tier), a small eval bundle comparing quality across quantization profiles, and a runbook for canary behavior. I’ll attach the sizing draft to the MAP.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Quick ops perspective / cost levers to include in the scenarios: 

- Dedicated pool vs shared hosted: dedicated gives predictable tail latency (recommended for the sub-100ms first-token target) — expect +25–40% cost vs shared but significantly lower p99.
- Autoscale + burst: configure aggressive scale-up for burst windows (60–180s) with burst capacity kept warm; this reduces cold starts but costs more in reserved v. pure burst.
- Continuous batching: expected token-cost savings 12–20% at steady-state. Latency hit depends on batch formation; recommend adaptive batching that relaxes target during spikes.
- Caching: presence of a prefix cache likely reduces downstream token count 15–25% — biggest win for repeated system prompts and templates.
- Quantization: int8 lowers GPU memory use and marginally lowers latency; 4-bit (if quality acceptable) can double concurrency for the same hardware.

I’ll turn these into concrete numbers in the XLS (20270601-inference-cost-model.xlsx) with three scenarios (conservative / balanced / aggressive). Ben will also include an estimate for the cost of keeping burst capacity warm for 2–3 high-traffic launch windows per quarter.

-Ben
